title: X OAuth 1.0a oauth_signature output and consumer-secret placeholders, references and masks
summary: An OAuth Authorization header and a query string that carry an oauth_signature derived value, a signing key written with a placeholder consumer secret, an environment reference, a masked display and prose that names the secret.
rationale: X documents the consumer secret as a secret input to the signing key, and the oauth_signature as the base64 form of the HMAC-SHA1 output of the signature base string and signing key, a derived output that is not the consumer secret (contract claim signing-key-input-signature-output). A placeholder, a reference or a mask in the signing-key position carries no value. The oauth_consumer_key is not used as a control because the pages do not call it public or secret (consumer-key-public-status). The case decides nothing about the oauth_signature as a confidential value, only that it is not the consumer secret.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are derived signature outputs, placeholders, references, masks or prose, not consumer secret values; that such forms are not values is a project decision, not an X statement. X documents the signing key as built from the consumer secret and the oauth_signature as its derived output.

sources.supports: In this case, the signing key should consist of the percent encoded consumer secret followed by an ampersand character ‘&’.
Finally, the signature is calculated by passing the signature base string and signing key to the HMAC-SHA1 hashing algorithm.
Both of these values need to be combined to form a signing key which will be used to generate the signature.
